title: The Body Foundations

learn.summary: Mood is built on physiology: sleep, movement, food, and light are the four levers with the largest, best-replicated effects on mental health. No thought technique compensates for chronic sleep deprivation. WHO guidance on mental health consistently lists physical activity and sleep among first-line self-care recommendations — start here before anything fancier.

do: Pick your single weakest foundation (sleep, movement, food, light) and improve only that one for the next two weeks. One lever, measured.

children.title: Sleep

learn.summary: Sleep deprivation amplifies amygdala reactivity to negative stimuli by around 60% (Matthew Walker's lab) — you are measurably more anxious and irritable on short sleep. Sleep hygiene basics with the strongest evidence: consistent wake time (even weekends), cool dark room, no caffeine within 8–10 hours of bed, and getting out of bed if you cannot sleep (stimulus control). Insomnia's gold-standard treatment is CBT-I, not medication.

do: Fix your wake time to within 30 minutes — all 7 days — for two weeks, and track how many nights you get 7+ hours.

children.title: Movement

learn.summary: Meta-analyses show exercise has antidepressant effects comparable to medication for mild-to-moderate depression, with benefits appearing at doses as low as brisk walking a few times a week. Mechanisms include BDNF release, reduced inflammation, and mastery experiences. The best exercise for mental health is the one you will actually repeat; intensity matters less than regularity.

do: Schedule three 20-minute brisk walks this week at specific times in your calendar. After each, rate your mood before and after (1–10).

children.title: Food & Mood

learn.summary: Nutritional psychiatry is young but real: the SMILES trial (Jacka, 2017) found a Mediterranean-style diet produced significant depression improvements versus social support alone. Mechanisms likely run through inflammation and the gut microbiome. The practical version is unglamorous — more whole foods, legumes, fish, and vegetables; fewer ultra-processed foods — plus noticing your personal blood-sugar-to-irritability pipeline.

do: For five days, jot your mood 1–10 two hours after each meal. Look for one food pattern worth changing.

children.title: Sunlight & Circadian Rhythm

learn.summary: Your circadian clock, seated in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, is set primarily by light hitting the eyes — and morning outdoor light (thousands of lux, versus ~300 indoors) anchors sleep timing, alertness, and mood. Bright-light therapy is a first-line treatment for seasonal affective disorder. Evening screens do the reverse: light at the wrong time delays melatonin and pushes the whole system later.

do: Get outside within an hour of waking for 10+ minutes on five days this week — no sunglasses needed, cloudy counts.
